analysis.answer: Current law sets a flat personal income tax rate of 6 percent. The measure lowers this rate to 5 percent for taxable years starting in 2028 or later.

The state will experience a direct loss in tax revenue. The opportunity cost is the public services, state workforce compensation, or infrastructure investments that would have been funded by that revenue.
Individuals and families with taxable income benefit by paying less in taxes. People and organizations relying on state-funded public services bear the cost of the reduced state revenue.

Taxpayers will retain more of their income, which they may allocate toward personal consumption or savings. The state government will face reduced revenue collections and may respond by cutting public services, increasing other taxes or fees, or drawing from reserves.

The measure addresses the financial burden of taxation on individuals by lowering the statutory tax rate. This mechanism directly reduces households' tax liability, but it may create a shortage of funding for state services.

It is empirically disputed whether cutting state personal income taxes stimulates enough economic growth to offset the resulting revenue losses. Some studies find that lower taxes attract businesses, investment, and high-income residents. Other research finds minimal growth effects and notes significant negative economic impacts when reduced tax revenue leads to cuts in public services like education and infrastructure.
